title: Finite cotensor corner preserves local acyclic fibrations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves and [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] for simplicial sets. Use [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps] for the homotopy-group and local-map conventions. For $V\in\mathcal C$, put $h_V(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,V)$. The simplex $\Delta^n$ is represented by $[n]$, its boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of its proper faces (empty when $n=0$), and $\Lambda_i^n$ is the union of the faces other than face $i$, for $n\ge1$ and $0\le i\le n$. Let $F,G:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves. A map $f:F\to G$ is a local Kan fibration if every commutative square from $h_V\times\Lambda_i^n\to h_V\times\Delta^n$ to $f$ has fillers after restriction along every arrow in some covering sieve of $V$; the fillers need not agree for different arrows. For objectwise Kan $F,G$, call $f$ a local weak equivalence if it induces an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for each $V\in\mathcal C$, $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, an isomorphism on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of $\pi_m(F|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(G|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$, where $\mathcal C/V$ has the induced topology. For a simplicial set $A$, define the objectwise cotensor by $(F^A)(V)_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(A\times\Delta^q,F(V))$. If $f$ is both a local Kan fibration and a local weak equivalence, and $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ is an inclusion of finite simplicial sets (finitely many nondegenerate simplices), then the objectwise cotensor corner map
$$F^L\longrightarrow F^K\times_{G^K}G^L$$
has objectwise Kan domain and codomain and is again a local Kan fibration and a local weak equivalence (hence a local acyclic fibration).

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, Proposition 3.3 (published numbering; v2 Proposition 3.3), Section 3, pp. 7-8; finite cotensor corner map.

proof.text: Set $H=F^L$ and $B=F^K\times_{G^K}G^L$. For each $V$, the internal-hom Kan theorem makes $H(V)$ and $F(V)^K$ Kan. Apply the corner-map theorem to $G(V)\to *$ and $K\hookrightarrow L$: restriction $r:G(V)^L\to G(V)^K$ is a Kan fibration. To fill a horn in $B(V)$, first extend its $F(V)^K$ coordinate using its Kan property. Compose that simplex with $f$ to obtain the prescribed base simplex in $G(V)^K$; the other coordinate on the horn and this simplex form a lifting square for $r$. A filler for $r$, paired with the first filler, is a filler in the degreewise pullback $B(V)$. Thus both $H$ and $B$ are objectwise Kan. This uses no objectwise-fibration hypothesis on $f$.

source.place: Propositions 3.2-3.3 and (3.4), printed pp. 7-8; direct finite-boundary-cell expansion of the acyclic case.

proof.text: Fix $m\geq0$ and put $D_m=\Delta^m\times L$ and $A_m=(\partial\Delta^m\times L)\cup(\Delta^m\times K)$, a degreewise union of simplicial subsets of $D_m$. The simplex $\Delta^m$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices: a map $[q]\to[m]$ is nondegenerate exactly when it is injective, since its epi-mono factorization gives a degeneracy whenever it is not injective. The finite-product theorem therefore makes $D_m$ finite. Apply the relative boundary-cell theorem to $A_m\hookrightarrow D_m$. Its cells are precisely the nondegenerate simplices of $D_m$ outside $A_m$. There are finitely many, so only finitely many dimension stages are nonempty, and each finite coproduct of attachments can be attached one summand at a time. Consequently there is a finite filtration $A_m=Z_0\hookrightarrow\cdots\hookrightarrow Z_N=D_m$, each map a pushout of one boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^{d_j}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{d_j}$, allowing $d_j=0$.

source.place: Propositions 3.2-3.3 and (3.4), printed pp. 7-8; direct finite-boundary-cell expansion of the acyclic case.

proof.text: The matching-cover theorem applied to $f$ supplies local strict boundary fillers in every degree, including degree zero. Consider any square $A_m\to F(V)$, $D_m\to G(V)$ for $f_V$. For the finite filtration just constructed, let $R_j$ be the sieve of arrows $u:W\to V$ on which this square has a partial lift $Z_j\to F(W)$ extending its prescribed $A_m$ map. Restriction of a partial lift shows that $R_j$ is a sieve, and $R_0$ is maximal. If $R_j$ covers, choose a partial lift for each $u\in R_j$. Its restriction to the next attaching boundary, together with the given simplex in $G(W)$, is a relative boundary section for $f$. The matching-cover theorem gives a covering sieve $T_u$ of $W$ where it extends strictly. Glue each filler to the partial lift by the pushout defining $Z_{j+1}$; hence $u^*R_{j+1}$ contains $T_u$ and covers. Covering sieves are upward closed by transitivity (the pullback of a larger sieve along any arrow of a smaller sieve is maximal). Transitivity along $R_j$ now proves that $R_{j+1}$ covers. Finite induction gives a covering lifting sieve $R_N$ for the whole square. No compatible choices on different arrows and no infinite intersection of covering sieves are used.

source.place: Propositions 3.2-3.3 and (3.4), printed pp. 7-8; direct finite-boundary-cell expansion of the acyclic case.

proof.text: Identify a relative boundary section for $H\to B$ over $V$ with a square as in the preceding step. Explicitly a map $Q\to F(V)^L$ corresponds to a map $L\times Q\to F(V)$: from $a:Q\to F(V)^L$ evaluate $a_q(z):L\times\Delta^q\to F(V)$ at $(l,\mathrm{id}_{[q]})$ on $(l,z)\in L_q\times Q_q$. Conversely a map $b:L\times Q\to F(V)$ sends $z\in Q_q$ to the composite $L\times\Delta^q\xrightarrow{1\times z}L\times Q\xrightarrow b F(V)$. These constructions are inverse and commute with simplicial operators. Thus a map $\partial\Delta^m\to H(V)$, and an $m$-simplex of $B(V)$ over its image, give maps $L\times\partial\Delta^m\to F(V)$ and $K\times\Delta^m\to F(V)$ agreeing on $K\times\partial\Delta^m$, and a map $L\times\Delta^m\to G(V)$ agreeing with their composites with $f_V$. Gluing the first two maps degreewise and swapping factors gives the square $A_m\to F(V)$, $D_m\to G(V)$. A strict lift of this square is exactly an $m$-simplex of $H(V)$ with the prescribed boundary and image. All formulas commute with restriction in $V$.

source.place: Propositions 3.2-3.3 and (3.4), printed pp. 7-8; direct finite-boundary-cell expansion of the acyclic case.

proof.text: For every relative boundary section of $H\to B$, Step 3 applied to the square identified in Step 4 gives a covering sieve with strict lifts. By the definition of generalized cover, every map $H_m\to\widetilde M_mH\times_{\widetilde M_mB}B_m$ is a generalized cover. Step 1 verifies that $H,B$ are objectwise Kan, so the boundary matching-cover criterion applies and proves that $H\to B$ is both a local Kan fibration and a local weak equivalence. For $m=0$, $A_0=K$ and $D_0=L$ and the identical argument uses the degree-zero boundary clause; no nonemptiness assumption has been imposed.

source.place: Propositions 3.2-3.3 and (3.4), printed pp. 7-8; direct finite-boundary-cell expansion of the acyclic case.

lean.statement: theorem cotensorCorner_local_acyclic_fibration {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet.{max u w}) (hF : ∀ V : C, SSet.KanComplex (F.obj (op V))) (hG : ∀ V : C, SSet.KanComplex (G.obj (op V))) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocalKanFibration J f) (hw : IsLocalWeakEquivalence J f) (K L : SSet.{max u w}) [SSet.Finite K] [SSet.Finite L] (i : K ⟶ L) [Mono i] : (∀ V : C, SSet.KanComplex ((F ⋙ ihom L).obj (op V))) ∧ (∀ V : C, SSet.KanComplex ((cotensorCornerTarget i f).obj (op V))) ∧ IsLocalKanFibration J (cotensorCorner i f) ∧ IsLocalWeakEquivalence J (cotensorCorner i f)
